timed_text.text: Day 24,
Most athletes aim for perfection.
Perfection is one of the most damaging standards to chase.
Here's a better target.
Raise your bottom line.
Here's what that means.
Every athlete has a range.
Their best days and their worst days.
The question isn't how high your ceiling is.
The question is, how high is your floor?
If your worst performance is at 60% of capability — that's your floor.
Athletes who compound commit to fundamentals until their floor rises.
Not their ceiling, their floor.
Their worst days become 75%, then 10, 85%.
Compounding happens through daily behaviors, not heroic game day efforts.
The routine, the evidence log, the reps you build when nobody's watching.
The commitment isn't to be perfect, it's to be reliable.
On screen — look at your current floor and commit to raising it.

cards.prompt: Honestly — what does your worst competitive performance look like right now? Not your fear of what it could be. What does it actually look like on a bad day?
What are the specific daily behaviors that, if you did them consistently, would raise that floor? Not the big things — the small, repeatable ones.
Commit to one behavior from that list that you will do every single day for the rest of this program — not because you feel like it, but because that's how the floor rises.

timed_text.text: Commit to your worst day being good enough.
Because when your floor is solid, your ceiling takes care of itself.
Go hit the journal and when you finish, day 24 is complete.

blocks.prompt: What would change about how you compete if you stopped chasing your best day and started committing to your most reliable day?
